# Connectivity Flow

Connectivity consists of four major parts:
<br>
1. ethernet
2. modem
3. wifi
4. ping

The fifth component if connectivity itself which extends the functionality provided by these
![image.png](data:image/png;base64,)

## Description
<br>
The first 3 components provide actual interfaces to connect to internet through the esp netif interface.
They have functions for:

1. Initializing the interface
2. Starting the connection
3. Stopping the connection

<br>
The fourth component of ping provides a way of checking if the underlying interface has internet availability.
It does that by starting a connection request through socketon the specified interface.
<br>
## Working
<br>
Connectivity itself provides functionality for switching to different interfaces.
It does this by getting a priority list from the user and deciding on started interfaces based on what number it is in the priority list and if it is providing internet access.

Connectivity provides override for \`internet availbility check\` only in case of single interface.
Wifi provides provisioning api due to presence of soft ap mode which is used exclusively for providing connection to wifi manager


## Usage

Usage is pretty straight forward.
Most of the things are controlled by menuconfig like enabling code for interface handling

sdkconfig settings
```
#
# Connectivity
#
CONFIG_ENABLE_WIFI=y
# CONFIG_ENABLE_ETHERNET is not set
# CONFIG_ENABLE_BLE is not set
# CONFIG_ENABLE_MODEM is not set
# CONFIG_ENABLE_GSM is not set
# end of Connectivity
```
These settings determine if the interface gets enabled or not.

c code
```
    init_connectivity(network_priority, false);
```

First argument is the priority which is just a list that determines what interface gets treated as primary and what gets treated as secondary.
```
 uint8_t priority[3] = {
     NETWORK_PROVIDER_WIFI,
     NETWORK_PROVIDER_NONE,
     NETWORK_PROVIDER_NONE
 };
```

Second argument is whether the user wants to provide external checks for internet availability. If this is false ping will be used as the internal check provider else the user needs to call this function to provide state change.
```
void connectivity_override_internet_availability(bool available);

```
NOTE: true is only allowed if only one interface is enabled.
